items.evidence: items.rs LootContext::condition() (line 1983) reads the kind ONLY from o.get("type") (line 1988); 1.21.11's 1,542 conditions all use the "condition" key (0 type-keyed), so every object-form condition's kind is "" and the match falls to _ => false. conditions() (line 2109) DOES consult the plural conditions array — every element fails. evaluate() applies pool["modifier"]/table["modifier"] (lines 1870-1871), expand() pushes e["modifier"] (line 2143), nested() applies entry["modifier"] (line 2284) — but 1.21.11's data has ZERO modifier keys and puts functions in functions arrays (983: 964 entry / 10 pool / 9 table). modifiers() (line 2298) HAS the dual-form discriminator (line 2308) — dead code, the container key is never read. Impact: 1,190 of 1,324 tables carry >=1 condition or >=1 function (blocks 1,050/1,083, entities 62/108, chests 54/56, gameplay 6/26, dispensers 3/3, equipment 3/3, spawners 3/5, shearing 3/22, harvest 2/3, archaeology 1/6, carve 1/1, charged_creeper 1/6, pots 1/1, brush 0/1); only 134 tables roll correctly. Path verified end to end: Game::block_loot_at (game.rs:3683) -> block_drops_by_player (items.rs:1559) -> block_drops_raw (items.rs:1620) -> ctx.evaluate (items.rs:1657/1671). Post-fix residual (recorded here, not a separate item): modifiers() has 12 arms and is missing 7 of the 19 function kinds (copy_components 71, furnace_smelt 16, set_enchantments 4, set_stew_effect 3, exploration_map 3, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier 3, set_instrument 1 — union 101 tables, verified disjoint fresh) and expand() has no minecraft:tag arm (loses the single tag entry in entities/creeper.json) — union + tag = 102 tables, exactly the 26.2 run's count.

items.evidence: horizon-world/src/loot.rs is written for the 26.3 loot format throughout: condition() (line 1368) reads c["type"] only (line 1377) while 1.21.11's 1,542 conditions use the "condition" key; modify() (line 1478) consults singular m["condition"] only (line 1488) while the 184 function-level condition lists are all plural; run() (line 1512) reads f["type"] only (line 1514) while the 1,404 functions use the "function" key (default _ => {} at line 1937); table_raw() (line 2021) checks singular pool["condition"] (line 2028) and applies pool["modifier"]/table["modifier"] (lines 2039, 2026) while 1.21.11 has 955 plural pool conditions arrays (incl. 6 nested in equipment/trial_chamber.json) and 0 modifier keys; expand() (line 2080) checks singular entry["condition"] (line 2081) while the 247 entry-level lists are all plural; create() (line 2131) applies entry["modifier"] (line 2133). The minecraft:tag arm reads entry["items"] (lines 2110, 2146) while 1.21.11's tag entry uses the name field. run() has 26 arms covering 15 of the 19 function kinds (missing only the block-only apply_bonus, copy_components, copy_state, explosion_decay) but they are unreachable on 1.21.11 data. Demonstrated live with the loot_fill example against the real prepared data (7 tables x seeds 1-5, evidence/loot_fill.txt, 153 lines): every stack count is 1 (set_count never runs); the gated music_disc_lava_chicken dropped on ALL 5 zombie seeds (the entity_properties + random_chance gate is never evaluated); blocks/stone -> minecraft:stone on all 5 seeds (vanilla: cobblestone without silk touch); blocks/diamond_ore -> minecraft:diamond_ore on all 5 seeds (vanilla: diamond); entities/creeper -> gunpowder x1 only on all 5 seeds (the tag entry never expands, set_count never applies); no enchantments anywhere (ancient-city books come out as plain minecraft:book, never enchanted_book). 0 additional gap checks: these tables are already counted under items.rs (B12-G01).

items.evidence: The 1.21.11 jar ships ZERO supports_* block tags and only two fluid tags (lava, water). The 1.21.11 template has NO synthesize_legacy_support_tags code anywhere (grep-verified). The frogspawn reads still point at the 26.x name and resolve to EMPTY sets in both survival implementations: block_survival.rs tag_states("minecraft:supports_frogspawn") (:609, block) and fluid_tag("minecraft:supports_frogspawn") (:619, fluid) — missing keys yield empty sets silently (tags.get(name).into_iter().flatten(), lines 482-497); level/survive.rs (:477-478) reads the same empty sets from the level Tags struct, whose resolve() defaults missing tags to empty (level/data.rs:398-400, .unwrap_or_default()). Vanilla 1.21.11's form, verified by javap -c on the 1.21.11 client-named jar (FrogspawnBlock.mayPlaceOn): the fluid below must be Fluids.WATER and the fluid above Fluids.EMPTY — no tag is involved. With both sets empty, frogspawn can never survive on water in the port. The other ten supports_* reads were verified fresh too and reproduce the same defect (sugar cane, cocoa, mangrove propagule, azalea, nether sprouts, nether wart — each block's vanilla 1.21.11 survival form javap-verified, none using a supports_* tag); they are Batch 5's scope in the merged ledger, recorded as evidence only. 0 gap checks in this run's tally (per the brief's reconciliation formula).

systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 5,096 data-driven files byte-identical to the 1.21.11 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. Every defect is code reading the 26.x form of a format 1.21.11 writes differently and failing silently — the same bug class as the 1.21.7 pilot's 26.x-tag findings (G1/G3/G5/G6), now in three places at once, and this run proves the defects live in the TEMPLATE itself: 1.21.10 inherited them line-for-line. (1) Loot keys — 1.21.11 writes the old forms (condition discriminator x1,542, function discriminator x1,404, plural conditions arrays x1,386, functions arrays x983, the tag entry's name field) while both engines read the 26.3 forms (type, modifier, singular condition, tag items). The type/modifier renames are 26.3 changes, and the 26.2 playtest fixes that taught the engines both forms were never carried to the template. (2) Survival tags — 1.21.11 has no supports_* tags at all; vanilla's survival checks use native tags (#dirt, #sand, #jungle_logs, #nylium) and hardcoded blocks (clay, soul sand, soul soil, mangrove leaves, water). The port adapted most checks to those native forms but left eleven reads pointing at 26.x names, and every one resolves to an empty set instead of failing loudly. (3) Motion/fluid-flow tags — the asset loader demands three 26.x-only tags with hard errors; 1.21.7's derivation fix was never carried, so the 1.21.11 client fails at the same startup point 1.21.7 did before its fix. The port DOES get the 1.21.11 forms right where it was written for them (specials hardcoded, cooking defaults per-type, transmute bounds pinned, spear trigger wired live). Vanilla also moved under the template in one place: breath_of_the_nautilus is genuinely new in 1.21.11, so a defect in 1.21.10 is correct behaviour here.
